skills.evidence: Solid programming fundamentals — able to read and predict the output of code
Practical SQL knowledge — correct SELECT/WHERE syntax, understanding of DELETE vs. TRUNCATE
Core data structures knowledge — arrays vs. linked lists, when to use a stack or a queue
Object-oriented programming fundamentals — inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes
Operating systems basics — what a process is, fundamentals of multithreading
Strong quantitative aptitude — time-and-work, ratios, percentages, and logical reasoning
Clear communication and a collaborative attitude — comfortable explaining your final-year project
Awareness of the software development lifecycle and the difference between Agile and Waterfall
Perform unit testing and collaborate closely with QA
Coursework or a project in banking/financial systems
